question: Pipe P can fill (5)/(6) part of a tank in 30 hours, and pipe Q can fill (3)/(4) part of the same tank in 27 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 2 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 4 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time for P to fill tank = 30 × (6/5) = 36 hours, Q = 27 × (4/3) = 36 hours.

Let total capacity = LCM(36, 36) = 36 units → Efficiency of P = 1, Efficiency of Q = 1.

In 2 hours, P and Q fill 2 × (1 + 1) = 4 units.

Pipe R empties these 4 units in 4 hours → Efficiency of R = −1 unit/hr.

Net efficiency (P + Q + R) = 1 + 1 − 1 = 1 unit/hr → Total time = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P can fill 5/6 part of the tank in 30 hours.

Q can fill 3/4 part of the tank in 27 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Net Efficiency = Sum of individual efficiencies

⇒ Time for Q to fill tank = 27 × (4/3) = 36 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 36 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Rule

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours, its efficiency is positive (1/x). If an outlet pipe empties it in y hours, its efficiency is negative (−1/y).

Net Rate of Filling

When multiple pipes operate together, the net rate of work is the algebraic sum of their individual rates.

Fractional Work

If a pipe fills a/b part of a tank in T hours, the total time required to fill the complete tank is T × (b/a) hours.
